clue.text: Indication submariner is surfacing

indicators.note: in a down clue, something surfacing rises from the bottom to the top, so the letters read upwards

blocks.note: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel

explanation.surface: A sign that a submarine commander is coming up from the deep.
explanation.walkthrough: The submariner is a specific fictional one, Captain Nemo; brought up the column, his name reads OMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or portent, something that points to what is going to happen.

clue.text: Raducanu's back, more confident one wants high returns

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of the tennis player's surname
comparative of sure

explanation.surface: Emma Raducanu returns from injury with more self-belief, hoping for big returns of serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Emma Raducanu is a British tennis player, which makes 'returns' look like tennis shots; here they are interest payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate interest, so profit on loans is exactly what such a lender demands.

clue.text: Around opening, one hammered sheet for platinum?

indicators.note: metal that is hammered is beaten out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order
one thing placed around another encloses it

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: Someone beats a sheet of platinum into shape around a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that platinum is not the metal but the anniversary: a platinum jubilee marks seventy years.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is the traditional label for a seventieth anniversary or jubilee, as in the late Queen's Platinum Jubilee.

clue.text: Spies a place where men go

blocks.note: taken as written
the gents is the British name for a men's public toilet

explanation.surface: A description of spies as somewhere men visit, like a club or bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' has its lavatorial sense: the gents is a men's public toilet in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Agents are operatives of a secret service, a standard synonym for spies.

clue.text: Chrome etc with a lot of rust on Sierras, oddly

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the word loses its tail
taking a word oddly keeps its odd-numbered letters: first, third, fifth and so on

blocks.note: rust as a colour is brown, cut short by its last letter
letters 1, 3, 5 and 7 of the word

explanation.surface: Chromed metal and similar finishes rusting on old Chevrolet Sierra pickups.
explanation.walkthrough: Chrome sounds like plating on a car, and Sierra is a pickup truck, but Chrome is Google's web software.
explanation.definitionFit: Google Chrome is one example of a web browser; 'etc' makes the definition plural, covering Firefox, Safari and the rest.

clue.text: Clap about engineers turning up fuel

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it
in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the clap is slang for gonorrhoea, a venereal disease, VD
the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Applause for the engineers who show up with the petrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clap' reads as applause but is slang for venereal disease. Derv is the British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Derv is diesel oil sold for road vehicles in Britain, so it is a kind of motor fuel.

clue.text: Speculators loudly vote for gold

indicators.note: something said loudly is heard, so it is the sound that counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: bulls are stock market speculators who buy expecting prices to rise
aye is a yes vote

explanation.surface: Market traders noisily back investing in bullion.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold here is not the metal but the centre ring of an archery target.
explanation.definitionFit: In archery the gold is the innermost scoring ring, the centre of the target, also called the bull's-eye.

clue.text: Large pole's covered in lead

indicators.note: something covered in another thing sits wrapped inside it

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as in clothing sizes
a snooker or billiards cue is a long tapering pole

explanation.surface: A big pole coated in the heavy metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests the metal Pb, but it means a pointer to the truth, as in a detective's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A lead in an investigation is a piece of evidence or hint that helps solve it, which is also a clue.

clue.text: Shambles! No good Queen covering up final note from Freddie Mercury

indicators.note: the final one of a run of letters is the last, so only the closing letter is kept
one piece covering up another sits on top of it, placed straight after it

blocks.note: a shambles is a mess
the last letter of the name
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A fan complains that Queen's cover version botches Freddie Mercury's last note.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen and Freddie Mercury pull toward the rock band, but Mercury is the Roman god, and Queen is just ER.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth Mercury carried messages for the gods, making him their herald and go-between.

clue.text: Match of variable quality

indicators.note: 'of' here means drawn from, so the letters come out of the words that follow

blocks.note: runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A game whose standard of play was uneven.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap between the two words, taking the last letter of one and the first four of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: To match something is to be its equal, as when one score or performance equals another.

clue.text: Brass still coating rupees from the east

indicators.note: a coating wraps round what it covers, so one piece encloses another
in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left

blocks.note: still and even both mean calm and level
R is the abbreviation for rupees

explanation.surface: Brass objects still wrapped in Indian banknotes arriving from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Brass means cheek or impudence, as in 'the brass neck to ask'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass and nerve are both informal words for impudent boldness or cheek.

clue.text: Breaking law, even US journalists must consider this

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it into pieces that can be put back differently

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: American reporters have to weigh up whether to break the law for a story.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as advice to the American press; the definition is the second half, describing what editors judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors weigh how newsworthy a story is before running it, which is precisely what the phrase denotes.

clue.text: Silver and such like? One investigates prices

blocks.note: a PI is a private investigator
rates are charges or prices

explanation.surface: A market analyst studying the price of silver and similar metals.
explanation.walkthrough: Silver is Long John Silver, the pirate in Treasure Island, not the precious metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the famous buccaneer of Stevenson's novel, so he and his kind are sea robbers.

clue.text: Leaders removing one dent in iron

indicators.note: removing something takes it away, so letters drop out of the word

blocks.note: presidents lead countries
Roman numeral
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bosses who take out a crease while ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I and DENT out of the middle of PRESIDENTS and the two ends close up.
explanation.definitionFit: To iron clothes is to press them, smoothing out creases with a hot flat plate.

clue.text: Look, I'm visibly happy to get picked up

indicators.note: something picked up by the ear is heard, so the sound matters rather than spelling

blocks.note: to beam is to smile broadly, showing happiness

explanation.surface: Someone delighted at being collected, telling everyone to see how pleased they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I beam' said out loud matches an old word for a glance.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyebeam is a literary or archaic word for a glance, a beam of sight from the eye.

clue.text: European queen with talent for being calm

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
QU is an abbreviation for queen
ability and talent are synonyms

explanation.surface: A continental monarch known for her gift of composure.
explanation.walkthrough: QU for queen, less common than ER or R, is the standard abbreviation in dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Equability is an even temper, a steady disposition that rarely gets upset or agitated.

clue.text: Made to run by header from Lucy Bronze?

indicators.note: a header is at the top, so only the first letter is taken
something set running is loosened and scattered, so the letters come back in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: A football chase set up by a header from England defender Lucy Bronze.
explanation.walkthrough: Lucy Bronze is an England women's footballer, so 'header' looks like a footballing move; Bronze, with its question mark, is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronze is the third-place award at the Olympics, one example of a medal, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Summon a naked malefactor to accept fine

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: Eve, naked in Eden, broke God's command by eating the forbidden fruit
OK means fine or all right

explanation.surface: Calling up an unclothed wrongdoer to take their punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' suggests a penalty, but it means all right. The naked wrongdoer is the biblical Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call up or conjure, as a memory or spirit is summoned into the mind.

clue.text: Start to lose heart after fan rejects intro from Lady Gaga

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter drops out
rejecting something throws it out, so letters are taken away
coming after means following, so one piece is placed behind the other

blocks.note: a fan or lover of something
the first letter of the word, to be removed
to found is to start or establish

explanation.surface: A devotee of Lady Gaga becomes disillusioned after skipping the opening number.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Gaga is not a unit: the fan loses Lady's L, and Gaga stands alone as the definition. FOUND loses its middle U.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gaga about someone means being infatuated, doting to excess, which is excessive affection.

clue.text: Grunts from pigs quietly going out

indicators.note: quietly is the musical piano abbreviation, and going means leaving, so that letter departs
out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Snorting noises coming from pigs as they softly leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Grunts sounds like the noise pigs make, but it is slang for infantry soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: In US military slang a grunt is an infantryman, and a GI is an American soldier.

clue.text: Copper Age road men rebuilt

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form

blocks.note: taken as written
RD is the abbreviation for road
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prehistoric route reconstructed by workmen from the Copper Age.
explanation.walkthrough: The Copper Age is a real prehistoric period, which hides that Copper alone is the definition, slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A gendarme is a French police officer, and copper is informal British slang for any policeman.

clue.text: German you sent west pocketing pound for tip

indicators.note: in an across clue, sending letters west runs them right to left
to pocket something is to take it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: du is the familiar German word for you
a pound is an enclosure for animals, as is a pen

explanation.surface: A German traveller sent off westward with a pound coin to leave as a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound and tip both look like money, but the pound is an animal enclosure and tip means overturn.
explanation.definitionFit: To tip something over is to turn it upside down, which is what upending it means.

clue.text: King, when retiring, strokes bird

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to pet an animal is to stroke it
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A monarch who, in retirement, pets a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen was King of England in the twelfth century, during the civil war called the Anarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen of Blois reigned as monarch of England from 1135 to 1154, one of its crowned rulers.

clue.text: Steel, say, was shown by artist beset by defamation

indicators.note: beset means surrounded on all sides, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the standard shorthand for an artist
libel is written defamation

explanation.surface: A steel sculpture put on display by an artist who faced a defamation suit.
explanation.walkthrough: Steel is David Steel, leader of Britain's Liberal Party from 1976 to 1988, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: David Steel led the UK Liberals, so he is one example of a member of that party.

clue.text: Criminal admitting racket in transported goods

indicators.note: admitting something lets it in, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: an old lag is British slang for a convict
a racket is a loud noise, a din

explanation.surface: A crook confessing to a smuggling scam involving shipped goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Racket suggests a criminal scheme, but it is simply noise. A lag is British slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Lading is the cargo or freight loaded aboard a ship, as in a bill of lading.

clue.text: Government, say, blocking revolutionary ruler

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word is turned back to front
blocking something stands in its middle, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: e.g., for example
an emir is a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: A government obstructing a ruler who has seized power by revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary ruler' reads as one figure, but revolutionary just turns the ruler round.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime is the government in power, especially an authoritarian one, the system of rule.

clue.text: Palladium rejected because screw contains iron

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so it is written backwards
to contain is to hold inside

blocks.note: as means because
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a screw is British prison slang for a warder or guard

explanation.surface: A metallurgist turns down palladium because the screw has iron in it.
explanation.walkthrough: Palladium and iron make this look like chemistry, but the Palladium was a statue of Pallas that was held to protect Troy. SA plus GUARD holds the iron.
explanation.definitionFit: A palladium, after the statue guarding Troy, is anything believed to give protection, which is a safeguard.

clue.text: Rifle butt might contain this

blocks.note: first meaning: to plunder or ransack, as with a captured town
second meaning: an old white wine like sherry, which a butt, a large cask, could hold

explanation.walkthrough: Rifle butt suggests a gun's stock; the butt is really a wine barrel, and sack is Falstaff's favourite fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to plunder it; sack was the Elizabethan name for dry Spanish sherry-type wine.

clue.text: Zest to put away doughnut or substantial puff

indicators.note: putting something away removes it from view, so letters are taken out

blocks.note: gusto is enthusiasm or zest
a ring doughnut is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Eating a doughnut with relish, or smoking a big cigar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' tempts as eating the doughnut, but it removes the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gust is a sudden strong blast of wind, a big puff of air.

clue.text: Left over fag rolled — it helps me think clearly

indicators.note: something rolled is turned round, so the word is written backwards

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
a fag is British slang for a cigarette, a cig

explanation.surface: A smoker with a leftover hand-rolled cigarette claiming it aids concentration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left over' reads as one phrase, leftover, but it is two separate abbreviations. Fag is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: Logic is the discipline of sound reasoning, so it is what lets someone reason clearly.

clue.text: More than one tin article in case of canvas

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Several metal items packed inside a canvas holdall.
explanation.walkthrough: The indefinite article is the short form before a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: A can is a tin container for food or drink, so several of them make plural tins.

clue.text: Moving spades, detect components of nickel

indicators.note: moving a letter shifts it from one end of the word to the other

blocks.note: to scent something is to detect it by smell

explanation.surface: Digging with shovels to find the parts that make up nickel ore.
explanation.walkthrough: Spades is the card-suit abbreviation S, moved from the front of SCENT to the back. Nickel sounds like the metal but is the US five-cent coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A US nickel is worth five of the smallest coins, so those units make up its value.

clue.text: Gag staff must keep wearing? This is irregular

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: to gag someone is to mute them
to staff something is to man it
wearing a garment is being in it

explanation.surface: A rule that employees must keep wearing masks or uniforms, and a complaint that the rule is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: Irregular is a noun here, a soldier outside the regular army, not an adjective about oddness.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutemen were American militia of the Revolutionary War, ready at a minute's notice, so irregular soldiers.
